name: Fermented papaya preparation
short: Blood sugar fell, with clinical signs, in people with type 2 diabetes on glibenclamide, who then cut their drug dose (one stopped it). Trial in 30 older adults: few adverse events, as placebo.
text: These data are for a fermented papaya preparation, a supplement made by fermenting Carica papaya, taken by mouth. Blood sugar: in a 2-month study in 25 people with type 2 diabetes taking the oral diabetes drug glibenclamide and 25 healthy people, all given the preparation daily, plasma sugar fell significantly in both groups; the hypoglycaemic effect, with clinical signs, led the diabetic patients to reduce the dose of their diabetes medicine, and in one patient it was stopped. On the other side, in a 6-week study of a higher daily amount in people with type 2 diabetes, aimed at its effect on high blood sugar, the abstract reports no influence on fasting glucose and the other blood measures studied, apart from an immune-cell measure. In a placebo-controlled crossover trial in 30 moderately functioning adults aged 70 to 100, with 8 weeks on each condition, there were no adverse changes in blood chemistries and few adverse events, not different from placebo, and no serious adverse effects in either condition. The beta-thalassaemia studies checked for this entry, including the one cited here, do not report adverse events in their abstracts. Interactions: in the glibenclamide study above, the fall in blood sugar led patients taking that medicine to reduce its dose; no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
